short: A milestone demonstration of sentence synthesis from ECoG, but its articulatory-intermediate claim is confounded by extra supervision and its intelligibility rests on closed word pools.
position: All three changed components are standard: sentence waveforms (M08) extend formant synthesis [[2]](#ref-2) and spectrogram decoding [[3]](#ref-3); mimed transfer (M04) repeats [[3]](#ref-3); the articulatory pipeline (M06) first implements a proposed architecture [[4]](#ref-4), with its benefit shown in one participant. Its lasting contribution is sentence synthesis from ECoG. The mechanistic claim does not hold as tested: the intermediate is the bottleneck of an encoder-decoder fed phoneme labels and the participant's own MFCCs, so the 0.54 dB gain over the direct decoder mixes articulation with extra supervision, and a later linear comparison found direct decoding slightly better [[5]](#ref-5). Intelligibility is overstated by closed word pools with no chance level. Whether articulatory structure, not added supervision, helps neural speech decoding remains untested.
